title: Erdős-Hajnal Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For every graph $H$, there exists $c>0$ such that in every $H$-free graph $G$ there is a clique or a stable set of size at least $|G|^{c}$.
context_text: Erdős and Hajnal conjectured this in 1977–1989; despite considerable attention the conjecture remains open. Until this paper, the only non-trivial prime graphs known to have the Erdős-Hajnal property were $P_4$, the bull, $C_5$, and (in progress) $P_5$.
paper_contribution: Proves infinitely many prime graphs satisfy the conjecture: all graphs $H$ whose every non-trivial prime induced subgraph $H'$ has a vertex of degree one and a vertex of degree $|H'|-2$; more generally, proves it whenever $H_1$ and $\overline{H_2}$ are both buildable (every prime induced subgraph with at least three vertices has a vertex of degree one).
paper_title: Induced subgraph density. IV. New graphs with the Erdős-Hajnal property

title: Polynomial Rödl Conjecture (Conjecture 1.7)
statement_text: For every graph $H$, there exists $d>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac{1}{2})$, and every $H$-free graph $G$, there is an $\varepsilon$-restricted subset of $V(G)$ with size at least $\varepsilon^{d}\lvert G\rvert$.
context_text: Fox and Sudakov conjectured this polynomial strengthening of Rödl's theorem. Taking $\varepsilon$ to be a small negative power of $n$ shows that Conjecture 1.7 implies the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture. Bucić, Fox, and Pham [4] later showed the Erdős-Hajnal property is equivalent to being viral (satisfying Conjecture 1.8), which implies Conjecture 1.7.
paper_contribution: The paper's results establishing the Erdős-Hajnal property for new (infinitely many prime) graph classes implicitly verify Conjecture 1.7 for those classes, via the equivalence proved by Bucić, Fox, and Pham.
paper_title: Induced subgraph density. IV. New graphs with the Erdős-Hajnal property

title: Conjecture 1.8
statement_text: For every graph $H$, there exists $d>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac{1}{2})$ and every graph $G$ with $\mathrm{ind}_{H}(G)\leq(\varepsilon^{d}\lvert G\rvert)^{\lvert H\rvert}$, there is an $\varepsilon$-restricted subset of $V(G)$ with size at least $\varepsilon^{d}\lvert G\rvert$.
context_text: Here $|G|$ is the number of vertices, a copy of $H$ in $G$ is an isomorphism from $H$ to an induced subgraph of $G$, $\mathrm{ind}_H(G)$ is the number of copies of $H$ in $G$, and $G$ is $H$-free if $\mathrm{ind}_H(G)=0$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)$, a graph is $\varepsilon$-restricted if it or its complement has maximum degree at most $\varepsilon$ times its number of vertices, and a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is $\varepsilon$-restricted if $G[S]$ is. Rödl's theorem says that for every $H$ and $\varepsilon$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every $H$-free graph has an $\varepsilon$-restricted subset of size at least $\delta|G|$; Nikiforov extended this to graphs with $\mathrm{ind}_H(G)\le(\delta|G|)^{|H|}$. Fox and Sudakov obtained $\delta=2^{-d(\log\frac1\varepsilon)^2}$ and conjectured the polynomial Rödl version $\delta=\varepsilon^d$ for $H$-free graphs, which implies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture (every $H$-free graph has a clique or stable set of size $|G|^{c}$ for some $c=c(H)>0$). This polynomial Nikiforov statement unifies both. A graph $H$ satisfying it is called viral, so the conjecture asserts that every graph is viral. Bucić, Fox and Pham proved that a graph has the Erdős–Hajnal property iff it is viral, so the conjecture is equivalent to the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The authors prove that every graph $H$ in which every prime induced subgraph $G'$ with $|G'|\ge3$ (prime meaning not obtainable from smaller graphs by vertex-substitution) has a vertex of degree one and a vertex of degree $|G'|-2$ is viral, giving infinitely many new prime graphs with the Erdős–Hajnal property.
paper_title: Induced subgraph density. IV. New graphs with the Erdős-Hajnal property
